Digitize the FISHMORPH reference workbook

Source: R/digitize_fishmorph_reference.R
digitize_fishmorph_reference.Rd

Opens the landmark digitizer of digitize_landmarks() on the FISHMORPH reference workbook (FISHMORPH_PUBLI_*.xlsx) instead of a campaign photo folder. It replaces Rfishmorph::launch_fishmorph_digitizer(): the same three queues, the same sheets, the same journal keys – and the application, the conventions checked on save, the ml-morph prediction and the append-only journal of the campaign digitizer, so the two kinds of work no longer run on two separately maintained tools.

Usage

digitize_fishmorph_reference(
  xlsx_path,
  photo_dir = file.path(dirname(xlsx_path), "Photos utilisees"),
  out_path = NULL,
  seg_sheet = "Global_segments",
  lm_sheet = "Global_Landmark",
  new_sheet = "New_specimen",
  new_photo_dir = file.path(dirname(xlsx_path), "Photos nouvelles"),
  ruler_mm = 10,
  journal_dir = file.path(dirname(xlsx_path), "landmark_journal"),
  operator = NULL,
  xlsx_flush_every = 10L,
  mode = c("reconstruct", "correct", "new"),
  mlmorph_dir = NULL,
  predictor = NULL,
  python = NULL,
  display = c("canvas", "plot"),
  launch.browser = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

xlsx_path

The FISHMORPH workbook (sheets seg_sheet and lm_sheet).

photo_dir

Folder of the species photographs. The default, Photos utilisees beside the workbook, is also found under its accented name Photos utilisées.

out_path

Working copy that is written. NULL (default): xlsx_path itself when its name ends in _reconstructed.xlsx, otherwise <name>_reconstructed.xlsx, created from xlsx_path if absent.

seg_sheet, lm_sheet, new_sheet

Sheet names: segments, landmarks, and the new specimens (created with the header of lm_sheet when absent). A sheet whose name differs only by case, separators or a final "s" (new_specimens / New_specimen) is recognised as the one asked for.

new_photo_dir

Folder of the new photographs (the "new" queue).

ruler_mm

Real length (mm) of the scale bar 20-21, "new" queue.

journal_dir

Journal folder. Default: landmark_journal beside the workbook – the folder the old digitizer used, so both histories are read together.

operator

Operator identifier (NULL: the system user).

xlsx_flush_every

Records between two writes of the workbook.

mode

Starting queue; switchable in the app.

mlmorph_dir, predictor, python

ml-morph resources, as in digitize_landmarks().

display

"canvas" (default, drawn in the browser) or "plot"; see digitize_landmarks().

launch.browser

Where the app opens (see digitize_landmarks()).

...

Passed to shiny::runApp().

Value

The path of the working copy, invisibly. Called for its side effect.

The three queues

  • "reconstruct": species WITHOUT landmarks, WITH segments and a photograph. Once the axis (1, then 2, with the hinges 22/24 on a curved fish) is placed, every landmark is seeded at the species' MEASURED proportions – its published segments – rather than at the median FISHMORPH proportions, so most of the work is checking.

  • "correct": rows ALREADY landmarked, on the landmark sheet or on the new-specimen sheet; their points are reloaded, to be reviewed and moved.

  • "new": the photographs of new_photo_dir, one entry per photograph, written to new_sheet (species name typed in the Species field, scale bar 20-21 optional).

What is written where

Every save is appended to the journal FIRST (the source of truth, read by landmark_journal_read() and consolidate_landmarks() together with the journals written by the old Rfishmorph digitizer), then to the working copy of the workbook (out_path), edited in place through openxlsx and written atomically every xlsx_flush_every records. The journal row_key is the species name ("reconstruct", "correct") or the photograph file name ("new"), as before, so the history of a species continues across the two tools. The quality score is on the common scale, 1 (unusable) to 5 (excellent), empty when not scored.

See also

digitize_landmarks(), landmark_journal_status(), landmark_journal_qc(), consolidate_landmarks()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
digitize_fishmorph_reference(
  xlsx_path     = "FishMORPH/FISHMORPH_PUBLI_9556sp_reconstructed.xlsx",
  photo_dir     = "FishMORPH/Photos utilisees",
  new_photo_dir = "FishMORPH/Photos nouvelles",
  operator      = "AT",
  mode          = "correct")
} # }
